subject: 100 Winchester Street Proposed Residential Development
overview: The development team presented a preliminary proposal for a 65-unit residential building at 100 Winchester Street under Medford’s new Planned Development District ordinance. The project includes underground parking, a commercial corner building restoration, and public landscaping, which residents discussed in relation to traffic safety and neighborhood character.

items.title: Planned Development District Overview
items.summary: Facilitators and city officials explained the Planned Development District (PDD) process, which allows for custom zoning overlays for specific projects through Community Development Board and City Council review.

items.title: Site Design and Architectural Presentation
items.summary: Architect Peter Quinn described the L-shaped, 65-unit building that steps down in height to respond to site slopes and includes two levels of underground parking with 50 spaces. The plan preserves a historic corner building to be restored for approximately 4,000 square feet of commercial use.

items.title: Landscape Architecture and Pocket Park
items.summary: The proposed landscape includes a formal entrance on Winchester Street, a woodland-style buffer on Alfred Street, and a public pocket park with seating at the corner of Winchester and Albion.

items.title: Public Q&A: Neighborhood Impacts
items.summary: Residents expressed concerns regarding traffic speeds on Winchester Street, the potential noise impact of a rooftop deck, and the management of trash and local rodent issues. Neighbors also suggested adding amenities such as car-sharing stations and co-working spaces for public use.

items.title: Residential Parking Restrictions
items.summary: Director of Planning Alicia Hunt stated that a likely condition for site plan approval would be prohibiting residents of the new development from obtaining street parking permits on Alfred Street.
